deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page is a working draft for Riemann's Paris prize essay on heat conduction, the 'Commentatio mathematica, qua respondere tentatur quaestioni ab Ill.ma Academia Parisiensi propositae' (submitted 1861, printed in the Werke 1876). The question it serves is when the heat equation of an anisotropic body can be transformed into one with constant coefficients.

(1) Variational form of anisotropic heat conduction. Riemann writes
  delta ∫∫∫ Σ_{i,j} a_{ij} u_{x_i} u_{x_j} dV + ∫∫∫ δu k u_t dV = 0.
The Euler–Lagrange equation is k u_t = 2 Σ ∂_i(a_{ij} ∂_j u). The factor 2 and the sign depend on how the first term is normalised.

(2) Change of variables s_μ = s_μ(x,y,z). Put P = (∂s_μ/∂x_i) and J = det P (Riemann's Σ ± ∂s1/∂x ∂s2/∂y ∂s3/∂z). Then:
- b_{μν} = Σ_{ij} a_{ij} (∂s_μ/∂x_i)(∂s_ν/∂x_j) / J, i.e. b = P a P^T / J.
- K = k/J.
- The variational principle keeps the same form in the s-variables, with b and K replacing a and k.

(3) Adjugates. Riemann writes β_{33} = b11 b22 − b12^2 and β_{23} = b12 b13 − b11 b23. These are the cofactors of the symmetric matrix b; similarly α is the cofactor matrix of a.
- Implicit step (mine): adj(P a P^T) = J^2 P^{-T} adj(a) P^{-1}. Hence β = P^{-T} α P^{-1}, i.e. β_{μν} = Σ α_{ij} (∂x_i/∂s_μ)(∂x_j/∂s_ν).
- This is what the written expansions show: β_33 = α_33 (∂z/∂s3)^2 + 2 α_23 (∂z/∂s3)(∂y/∂s3) + ..., with α_33 = a11 a22 − a12^2 and α_23 = a12 a13 − a11 a23. Only the first terms are written out.
- Consequence: Σ α dx dx = Σ β ds ds. The inverse (cofactor) form of the conductivity matrix transforms like a line element, with no Jacobian factor.
- Determinants: A = Σ a_{1j} α_{1j} = det a. Since det b = det(a) J^2 / J^3, we get A = J·B. Combined with K = k/J this gives k/A = K/B.
- So the problem reduces to: when can the quadratic differential form Σ α dx dx be brought to constant coefficients?

(4) Geodesics of Σ α dx dx. Riemann takes δ∫ sqrt(Σ α_{ιι'} dx_ι dx_ι'), expands the variation and integrates by parts (the term −2 δx d Σ α dx/ds). With arc length as parameter this gives
  Σ_ι α_{ιι'} x''_ι + Σ ∂α_{ιι'}/∂x_{ι''} x'_ι x'_{ι''} = ½ Σ ∂α_{ιι''}/∂x_{ι'} x'_ι x'_{ι''}.
Multiplying by the cofactors of α gives A x''_{ι'''} + ... . This uses adj(α) = A·a, an implicit step (mine). Riemann also notes the invariance identities Σα dx dx = Σβ ds ds, Σα dx δx = Σβ ds δs and Σα δx δx = Σβ δs δs.

(5) The curvature (flatness) test. Riemann forms the invariant second-variation expression
  δδ Σ β ds ds − 2 dδ Σ β ds δs + dd Σ β δs δs.
His leading term is
  (∂²β_{ιι}/∂s_{ι'}² − 2 ∂²β_{ιι'}/∂s_ι∂s_{ι'} + ∂²β_{ι'ι'}/∂s_ι²)(ds_ι δs_{ι'} − ds_{ι'} δs_ι)^2.
This is the second-derivative part of the Riemann curvature quadrilinear form (ιι', ι''ι''') of the Commentatio, evaluated on the bivector ds ∧ δs.

(6) Explicit expansion for a general metric Σ a ds ds (a now denotes the metric coefficients). He imposes geodesic-type normalisations on the second differentials, of the form Σ a_{ιι'} d²s_{ι'} = ½ Σ p ds ds, with analogous conditions for δ²s and dδs. Here p is a Christoffel-type combination of first derivatives. He then expands, with d and δ commuting:
- Terms in ∂²a: coefficient 4 ds ds' δs δs' − 2(ds δs' + δs ds')(ds'' δs''' + δs'' ds''') + 4 δs δs' ds'' ds'''. This is 4 times the second-derivative part.
- Terms in ∂a: products of first and second differentials.
- Terms in a: the third-order differentials cancel by symmetry of a, leaving Σ a (4 δds_ι δds_{ι'} − 2 d²s_ι δ²s_{ι'} − 2 d²s_{ι'} δ²s_ι).
These are to be eliminated with the normalisations, which produces the quadratic p-terms of the curvature.

(7) Last lines. He begins product-rule expansions of d Σ a δs δ's, δ Σ a ds δ's and δ' Σ a ds δs. These are the preparation for a symmetric computation with three variations.
errors: Normalisation of the a-terms in (6): computing δδ − 2dδ + dd literally gives 2Σa(δds δds' − d²s δ²s') for the a-part, i.e. 4Σaδdsδds' − 2Σa(d²sδ²s' + d²s'δ²s) after doubling. The ∂²a-part, however, is written at 4 times its value. If the reading is right, the a-terms are at twice their value rather than four times, a factor-2 inconsistency. The manuscript is heavily corrected here and the crossed '½' suggests the normalisation was still in flux, so this is tentative.
The β_{33} and β_{23} expansions in terms of ∂x/∂s are incomplete: only the first one or two terms are written. They are consistent with the correct law β = P^{-T} α P^{-1}.
In the curvature-term line the overall sign and the factor relative to Riemann's later (ιι',ι''ι''') are not fixed here. This is a draft, not an error of substance.
The 2 → −2 correction in the ∂a-coefficient line is a self-correction by Riemann; the result is consistent with the expansion of −2dδ.

results.what: Transformation law of the anisotropic heat-conduction variational principle under change of coordinates: b = P a P^T / J and K = k/J.
results.modern_name: Covariance of a divergence-form elliptic/parabolic operator (pullback of a conductivity tensor density)

results.what: The cofactor (inverse) form Σ α dx dx transforms like a line element, and k/A = K/B is invariant; this reduces the problem to equivalence of quadratic differential forms.
results.modern_name: Inverse conductivity tensor as a Riemannian metric (conductivity-to-metric correspondence)

results.what: Geodesic equations of Σ α dx dx, solved for x'' using cofactors.
results.usually_credited_to: Euler/Lagrange; in general n-dimensional form Riemann, Christoffel 1869

results.what: Invariant δδΣ − 2dδΣ + ddΣ and its leading term (ds δs' − ds' δs)^2 times second derivatives of the metric, as the criterion for flatness.
results.modern_name: Riemann curvature tensor / sectional curvature on the bivector ds∧δs

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a working draft of Riemann's known Paris prize Commentatio (1861, published in the Werke 1876 with Dedekind/Weber notes). It contains the transformation of the conductivity form, the geodesic equations, and the δδ−2dδ+dd expression giving the curvature tensor. All of this is famously Riemann's; the page only adds draft-level detail of the computation.

checkable.sympy: P=Matrix(3,3,symbols('p0:9')); a=Matrix(3,3,lambda i,j: Symbol('a%d%d'%(min(i,j),max(i,j)))); J=P.det(); b=P*a*P.T/J; simplify(b.adjugate() - (P.inv().T*a.adjugate()*P.inv())) == zeros(3,3)
checkable.asserts: The adjugate β of b = P a P^T/J equals P^{-T} α P^{-1}, so Σβ ds ds = Σα dx dx.
B = A/J, i.e. A = J·B, and hence k/A = K/B with K = k/J.
β_{23} = b12 b13 − b11 b23 is the (2,3) cofactor of a symmetric matrix.
adj(α) = A·a for 3x3 matrices, as used to solve the geodesic equations for x''.
For a conformal 2D metric, the Euler–Lagrange equation of Σα x'x' has the form Σα x'' + Σ∂α/∂x x'x' = ½ Σ ∂α/∂x x'x' (up to a factor of −2), as written by Riemann.

transcription_corrections: The three normalisation conditions in the boxed group are best read as Σa d²s = ½Σp ds ds, Σa dδs = ½Σp ds δs, Σa δ²s = ½Σp δs δs. The machine transcription gives δ²s twice.
Above the β lines Riemann labels the factors α_{3,3}, α_{2,3} and β_{2,3}, β_{3,3}, identifying the bracketed coefficients as cofactors of a.
In the β_{2,3} line the right-hand side is (a11a22−a12^2)(∂z/∂s3)(∂z/∂s2) + ..., i.e. only the α_33 term is written.
In the ∂a-coefficient line the sign '2' is corrected to '−2' (the '−2' written below the line), as indicated.
The leading '½' before δδΣβ ds ds is struck out in the manuscript.
